witness.description: Concrete instance certifying the exact-ℚ behavior claimed by L1: a fixed batch of linear rational claims over ℚ, a malformed input (float literal) and a sign-failing input. The witness is the dict passed to verify(witness); no I/O of any kind.

claim: FRAGMENT of L1: verify(witness) raises on any failed check and returns True only when (i) every linear rational claim in the batch holds exactly over Fraction, (ii) the float-literal input aborts at ingestion (no non-ℚ path), and (iii) the trivial 0==0 sign-failing input aborts fail-closed — the behavioral content of L1 instantiated to these inputs; the universal claim over all inputs is not machine-certified here.
law: Wang 7.2: an exact finite object plus a proved reduction is a CERTIFICATE. The reduction is the `claim` and is a human's to audit; the object and the verifier run are the machine's part.
